L158: When trying to parse `(calc(true))`, e.g. a @support feature query of the form InParens(GeneralEnclosed), the parser doesn't appear to consume the outer close parenthesis if you don't parse the inner block.
L159: This doesn't work:
L160: 
L161:     #[test]
L162:     fn outer_block_end_consumed() {
L163:         let mut input = Parser::new("(calc(true))");
L164:         assert!(input.expect_parenthesis_block().is_ok());
L165:         assert!(input.parse_nested_block(|input| input.expect_function_matching("calc")).is_ok());
L166:         assert_eq!(input.next(), Err(()));
L167:     }
L168:     thread 'tests::outer_block_end_consumed' panicked at 'assertion failed: `(left == right) && (right == left)` (left: `Ok(CloseParenthesis)`, right: `Err(())`)', src/tests.rs:268
L169: This does work:
L170: 
L171:     #[test]
L172:     fn outer_block_end_consumed() {
L173:         let mut input = Parser::new("(calc(true))");
L174:         assert!(input.expect_parenthesis_block().is_ok());
L175:         assert!(input.parse_nested_block(|input| {
L176:             try!(input.expect_function_matching("calc"));
L177:             input.expect_no_error_token()
L178:         }).is_ok());
L179:         assert_eq!(input.next(), Err(()));
L180:     }
L181: 
L182:     test tests::outer_block_end_consumed ... ok
